Thanks for the context, Stephanie — and thanks Luis for the note.

Short answer: yes, procurement can permit a temporary invoice-only onboarding for sandbox/trial activity under specific controls. Proposed guardrails below: 

- Eligibility: vendor must provide a completed W-9, primary billing contact, and an expected spend estimate < $3,000/month for the exception window.
- Security: for sandbox access we accept a one-page security attestation (self-attestation) that there is no access to production systems and no sensitive customer data will be sent to Redwood during the trial. If the integration will process customer data or PII, we require a higher bar (SOC 2 report or equivalent).
- Term & cap: 90-day temporary allowance by default with automatic review at day 45. Monthly cap set at $3,000; any projected overage requires pre-approval and conversion to PO-backed onboarding.
- Evidence & intake: complete procurement_exception_form.pdf (I attached a stub), attach W-9 and billing contact, and confirm the security attestation. Procurement will run a quick risk check (24–48 hours) once documents are submitted.
- Finance ops: finance needs to enable an invoice-only billing code and set up monthly invoice generation. I will loop finance in once procurement sign-off is recorded.

Next steps for this thread: if MerchantLabs confirms they will provide W-9 + attestation, Stephanie/Marissa — please route the documents to procurement@redwood.com. We'll queue the risk check and, if green, issue the 90-day allowlist authorization and notify finance to enable monthly invoicing.

I have some precedent templates for the attestation and the exception form — attaching procurement_exception_form.pdf.

-David
